DATA-QUALITY FLAG (not a DB conflict, since the field is null, but worth a reviewer's attention): the existing DB value drive_type='Straddle Stacker' sits oddly next to this datasheet's explicit claim of 'freitragende Gabeln' (free-floating/cantilever forks, i.e. nothing protrudes under the load) on p.2-3 of the factsheet -- per the industry README (Sec. 6) a straddle-under-load design is exactly the design that CANNOT handle closed-bottom pallets, which is the opposite of what free-floating forks imply. Also note existing DB value special_fork_option='Standard Fork' is not a valid AP0 allowed_value for that field (allowed=['Telescopic','Side-Shift','Clamp']) -- pre-existing data-quality issue, not introduced by this run, left untouched since it is non-null.

products.notes: NEW PRODUCT, not previously in DB (no EAE-series product existed). Genuinely new Jungheinrich 'Niederhub' (low-lift) Mobile Robot model, distinct from the existing low-lift BT Levio LAE250 (lifting_height=120mm, drive_type='Pallet Mover') and from ERE 225a (lifting_height=125mm) -- EAE 212a has 250mm lift and only 1200kg payload, positioning it as a smaller/lighter unit than either. product_type set to Forklift AGV by analogy with LAE250/ERE225a (same low-lift pallet-truck category), though the source material calls it a 'Mobile Robot' throughout rather than 'FTF' (Fahrerloses Transportfahrzeug) like the ERC/ERE lines -- worth a second look if the Tech Lead wants a stricter distinction. drive_type intentionally left null: unlike EKS 215a's explicit 'freitragende Gabeln' (free-floating forks) claim, this document only says the vehicle can also pick up 'manuell bereitgestellte Ladehilfsmittel' (manually provided load carriers) without stating whether it is underride or cantilever-fork design -- genuinely ambiguous, not guessed. vehicle_length/vehicle_width not stated anywhere in either source file (only the summary table's 5 columns: payload/lift/speed/lift-speed/height) -- left null. vda5050_compatible flagged above as inferred from the family pattern rather than a literal sentence in this specific document -- the safer, more literal alternative would be to leave it null pending a direct re-check; kept as true per the very strong Jungheinrich Mobile-Robot-line pattern (5/5 other Jungheinrich Mobile Robot lines processed this batch state it explicitly and identically) but flagged for a fast confirmation pass.
